podcast.title: Naming Fictional Band "Citizen Dick"
podcast.body: Jeff Ament was tasked with coming up with a name for a fictional band that he, Eddie Vedder, Stone Gossard, and actor Matt Dillon would be part of in the movie *Singles*. From his list of options, "Citizen Dick" was selected as the winning name. "Jeff Amit had been given the task of coming up with a name for a fictional band that he, Eddie and Stone and Matt Dillon, one of the stars of the film, would be in, so he listed a bunch of options."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Origin of "Spoonman" Name
podcast.body: One of the alternative names Jeff Ament considered for the fictional band in *Singles* was a song named after "Artis," a street performer who played the spoons. This idea later contributed to Chris Cornell's development of the song "Spoonman." "But one of the other options was a song named after a street performer named Artis who played the Spoons."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Formation Origin - Pickup Basketball Game (1989)
xref.body: The band's genesis began in Seattle when Stone Gossard and Jeff Ament formed Love Company and sought a singer by circulating a demo. Jack Irons, a former Red Hot Chili Peppers drummer, received a copy of this demo and passed it to Eddie Vedder, a surfer and night shift worker at a Chevron tank farm in San Diego, after a pickup basketball game in 1989. Eddie then wrote lyrics to three of the demo's five songs, dubbed them onto a new cassette, and sent it to Seattle, leading to his invitation to jam with the group and the formation of Pearl Jam. "This cassette passed out of a gym bag sometime in 1989 might have resulted in the most profitable pickup basketball game ever played."

xref.title: Singles Cameo (1992) – Eddie, Stone, and Jeff as Citizen Dick Members
xref.body: In Cameron Crowe's Seattle-set film *Singles* (filmed 1991, released 1992), Eddie Vedder, Stone Gossard, and Jeff Ament appear as the backing band for fictional singer Cliff Poncier (played by Matt Dillon), in a band called Citizen Dick. Their longest appearance is just over a minute, showing them reading a review of their record. By the time the film was released, Pearl Jam was enormous, which worked greatly in the film's favor. Pearl Jam also contributed two songs to the soundtrack: "Breath" and "State of Love and Trust." "By the time the movie was released in 1992, the band was huge."

xref.title: "Vs." Anti-System Release Strategy
xref.body: Pearl Jam deliberately released *Vs.* in stages, with the vinyl edition first appearing in the UK on October 11, 1993, followed by North America on October 12. The CD and cassette versions were delayed until October 18 and 19, respectively. This staggered release was a conscious effort by the band to "mess with the system" and "stick it to the label," Epic Records, which they felt was trying to kill off vinyl in favor of more expensive and profitable CDs. In 1993, none of the band members even owned a CD player, and Jeff Ament preferred a cassette version as his primary listening format. Further challenging the label, the vinyl edition was released without the album title or band name printed on it, forcing Epic to add a sticker to the shrink wrap. "Why? Phil Jim just wanted to mess with the system. So they did. In their mind, it was another way to stick it to the label."

xref.title: Band Disintegration after Singer's Death
xref.body: Mother Love Bone dissolved after their singer, Andrew Wood, died from a heroin overdose. This event led Stone Gossard and Jeff Ament to seek new musical projects, eventually leading to the formation of what would become Pearl Jam. "Stone and Jeff were looking for something to do after their band Mother Love Bone fell apart when their singer Andrew Wood died of a heroin overdose."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Catalyst for Pearl Jam
xref.body: The musicians who participated in the Temple of the Dog recording sessions enjoyed their time together, leading Mother Love Bone's bassist Jeff Ament and guitarist Stone Gossard to decide to continue working together, eventually forming Pearl Jam with Mike McCready and Eddie Vedder. "Most of the musicians who took part in the Temple of the Dog Sessions really had a good time hanging out. And when the record was finished, Mother Love Bone's bassist and guitarist decided to stick together."

xref.title: Deep Six Compilation Appearance
xref.body: Green River was featured on the "Deep Six" compilation, an important record for the Seattle scene. The band included guitarist Jeff Ament, who would later form Pearl Jam, and Mark Arm, who had a day job at MuZac Corporation. "Other groups to appear on the Deep Six compilation included a new band called Soundgarden, a band called Green River featuring guitarist Jeff Amit, who would later go on to a former group called Pearl Jam."

xref.title: Eddie Vedder's Audition Tape Creation
xref.body: After receiving a demo tape from Jack Irons, Eddie Vedder listened to it repeatedly. Following a night shift and a surfing session, he sat down at home and wrote lyrics for three of the five songs on the tape. He then recorded his vocals and the new lyrics onto a cassette and mailed it to Seattle, where Jeff Ament and Stone Gossard immediately recognized his talent, solidifying his role as their frontman. "As soon as Eddie got the tape from Jack, he started listening to it over and over."

xref.title: Formation and Major Label Debut
xref.body: Pearl Jam was formed as a result of the fallout from the band Mother Love Bone, and they proceeded to sign directly with a major label. Jeff Ament, a member of Green River, was a part of this formation. "And then there was the Fallout from Mother Love Bone, which eventually resulted in the formation of Pearl Jam, who also went right to a major."

xref.title: Formation from Mother Love Bone and Temple of the Dog
xref.body: Pearl Jam was formed by Mother Love Bone's bassist Jeff Ament and guitarist Stone Gossard, who decided to continue playing together after the Temple of the Dog sessions. They were joined by guitarist Mike McCready, a veteran of several small Seattle groups, and singer Eddie Vedder, who had moved from San Diego to perform background vocals on the Temple of the Dog record. "Jeff Ammett and Stone Gossard were joined by guitarist Mike McCready, a veteran of several small Seattle groups. And for a singer, they chose this skinny surfer dude who had moved up from San Diego to do background vocals on the Temple of the Dog record. His name was Eddie Vetter and the result of course was Pearl Jam."

xref.title: Legacy and Band Spin-offs
xref.body: Following Andrew Wood's death, the surviving members, bassist Jeff Ament and guitarist Stone Gossard, along with friends from Soundgarden, formed Temple of the Dog to record a memorial album. The positive experience of these sessions eventually led Ament and Gossard to form Pearl Jam. "Some of the surviving members of Mother Love Bone got together with friends from Soundgarden, a few other local musicians to record an album in Andrew's memory."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Members' Future Bands
xref.body: After the Temple of the Dog album was released, Chris Cornell and Matt Cameron were active in Soundgarden, while Stone Gossard, Jeff Ament, Mike McCready, and Eddie Vedder formed Pearl Jam. "By the time that Temple of Dog album came out, Chris Cornell and Matt Cameron were doing well in Soundgarden, while the other guys in the group stayed together in Formed Pearl Jam."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Members' Future Success
xref.body: Guitarist Jeff Ament, a member of Green River, later went on to form Pearl Jam, a highly successful grunge band. Another member, Mark Arm, worked at the Musak Corporation warehouse and is credited with coining the term "Pure Grunge" in a letter, marking the first known use of the "G-word" for the Seattle sound. "Another group called Green River featuring guitarist Jeff Ament, who would later go onto form a group called Pearl Jam. Another member of Green River was Mark Arm."

xref.title: Predecessor to Pearl Jam – Formation with Eddie Vedder
xref.body: Mookie Blaylock was the original name of the band formed by Mother Love Bone's Jeff Ament and Stone Gossard, who invited a young singer named Eddie Vedder from San Diego to join. The band quickly changed its name to Pearl Jam, which went on to achieve massive success. "This kid from San Diego who had just flown up at the invitation of Jeff and Stone to sing in a new band that was going to be called Mookie Blaylock, and that kid's name was Eddie Vedder."

xref.title: Transformation into Pearl Jam – Post-Tragedy Rebirth
xref.body: Following the tragic death of Andrew Wood, the surviving members of Mother Love Bone, Jeff Ament and Stone Gossard, collaborated with Chris Cornell and Matt Cameron to form Temple of the Dog. This collaboration eventually led Ament and Gossard to form a new band with Eddie Vedder, initially called Mookie Blaylock, which soon became Pearl Jam. "When Mother Lovebone collapsed and turned into Pearl Jam, Kelly became their full-time manager, leaving Susan to deal with Allison Chains."
